subject: Phased multi-year amendment: 3yr ramp + co-term exit windows
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Liu <susan.liu@nimbleai.com>
Cc: NimbleAI Procurement <procurement@nimbleai.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Phased multi-year amendment: 3yr ramp + co-term exit windows

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I put together a short proposal that lets NimbleAI lock-in a 3-year committed path while preserving operational flexibility during year 1 and an explicit co-term/exit window at the 18-month mark. High level: 

- Year 1: phased ramp (50% commit months 1-6, 75% months 7-12) with burst credits for unexpected spikes.
- Year 2–3: stepped annual commitments with predictable renewal pricing.
- Auto-renew: optional auto-renew with 60-day opt-out and a one-time right to convert to consumption pricing within the first 90 days of year 2 (to reduce risk).

Attached is a short draft amendment (draft_amendment_v1.pdf) showing proposed language and the pricing matrix. Key asks from you so I can move to Legal/Finance: 1) confirm target start date, 2) any procurement timing constraints, and 3) whether NimbleAI needs a co-term with an existing vendor contract.

If that looks generally right I can loop in Marissa (pricing/legal) and Priya (CS onboarding) for redlines and an updated DocuSign.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0124

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A few quick clarifications before you loop Legal: 

1) The Year 1 ramp math — can you show the expected monthly token allowance vs our average baseline so we can model burn?
2) The 60-day auto-renew opt-out: procurement prefers a 30-day opt-out for multi-year commitments. Is that negotiable?
3) The co-term/exit at 18 months: will that trigger any early termination fees, or is it a clean exit with a proportional refund of unused credits?

I attached our procurement calendar (procurement_timeline_q3.pdf) — we need final contract by 2027-04-20 to hit our internal Q2 budget cycle.

I can pull Michael (engineering/ops) in if you want technical guardrails for burst capacity.

Thanks,
Susan

Marissa / Priya —

Forwarding Susan's questions (see below). Procurement wants a faster sign-off cadence (final by 2027-04-20). Can you: 

- Marissa: update the pricing spreadsheet with month-by-month token allowances for Year 1 (baseline vs proposed ramp) and show cost delta for 30-day vs 60-day opt-out.
- Priya: confirm onboarding timeline assumptions and whether the 18-month exit would impact playbook deliverables.

If Legal needs specific language for a non-punitive exit, Marissa, can you draft a redline (we often use a proportional credit calculation: unused committed token value refunded pro rata less a 10% administrative offset)? Use conservative language but keep customer-friendly.

I'll keep Susan and procurement in loop.

Thanks —
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Susan Liu <susan.liu@nimbleai.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased multi-year amendment: 3yr ramp + co-term exit windows

Ben / Susan / Priya —

Attached is an initial redline (redline_amendment.docx) and a pricing model (pricing_model_v2.xlsx) that spells out month-by-month token allocations for Year 1 based on the 50%→75% ramp. Highlights: 

- We modeled three baseline scenarios (low/median/high) and included a conservative buffer for burst credits; the spreadsheet shows nominal overage thresholds and unit prices.
- For the auto-renew opt-out: our standard is 60 days for committed contracts; reducing to 30 days increases unit price ~4.8% across the tranche. I flagged the delta in the pricing tab.
- Exit mechanics at 18 months: legal suggests a proportional credit refund with an administrative offset of 7.5% (we can push to 5% as concession). No early termination penalty beyond the credit reconciliation.

Next steps: Ben, if Nimble prefers the 30-day opt-out, we can present a counter with the 4.8% uplift and highlight the one-time conversion right in year 2 as additional protection. Priya, I noted key onboarding milestones that might slip by 2–3 weeks if Nimble leans on high-burst usage in months 1–3.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Proposal update + DocuSign (option: 30d opt-out with uplift)

Susan / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick review. Per Marissa's modeling, I've attached the updated pricing model and a redlined amendment. Two options for you to review: 

A) 60-day opt-out (standard): no price change, 7.5% admin offset on prorated refunds for early exit.
B) 30-day opt-out (procurement-preferred): 4.8% unit price uplift; 5% admin offset on prorated refunds; same 18-month clean exit mechanics.

I've opened a DocuSign envelope for Option B (shorter opt-out) to speed procurement if you'd like to take that route: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/ABCDEF

Proposed next steps: 
- If you want Option B, sign DocuSign and we target 2027-04-01 effective date so onboarding can start mid-April (meets your Q2 window).
- If you prefer Option A, reply-all with confirmation and we'll send the standard amendment for sign.

Ben
